Choosing a sourdough starter

Subscribe
Overview Comments Related

A sourdough starter is a flour and water paste that keeps a living culture of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria. Feed it equal weights of flour and water once a day and it is ready to bake with when it doubles in size within six hours.

Rye flour ferments faster than white flour, so many bakers begin a new starter with a spoonful of rye. Keep the jar at about 24 degrees Celsius for the most predictable rise.

A starter that smells of nail polish remover is hungry. Feed it more often, or keep it somewhere cooler.
